purpose: Scoped, single-operation evidence for ONE governed rebind of the single staging public.communication_provider_accounts row (meta_whatsapp_cloud / whatsapp) from the PRODUCTION Meta asset references to the dedicated STAGING ones. It exists because the audited 40.12 seed correctly refuses this repair — classifyExistingAccount() returns ABORT / ACCOUNT_IDENTITY_CONFLICT when both stored references are non-null and differ — and that conflict rule is a reusable safety property that must not be weakened to unblock one row.
privacy: Meta asset identities appear ONLY as SHA-256 digests of the raw id strings. The three PRODUCTION digests are deliberately NOT recorded here: they live only in the owner's external, role-labelled proof file, which is never copied into this repository. This matches the existing posture in docs/provider-manifests/meta-staging-one-shot-template-creation.json and meta-template-remote-state.json. No token, app secret, verify token, phone number, project ref or raw Meta id is recorded here.

relationship_to_audited_seed.note: The seed continues to ABORT with ACCOUNT_IDENTITY_CONFLICT on a divergent non-null binding, exactly as before. This one-shot authority is separate, targets one pinned row, and hands the NULL-reference case straight back to the seed's NORMALIZED_DISABLED path rather than duplicating it.

owner_authorization.rationale: The staging row was seeded on 2026-08-01 carrying the production WABA and phone references. That binding makes canaryActivationRuntime readAccount() — which filters on phone_number_reference — return null, yielding ACCOUNT_MISSING at plan time, and it leaves production asset identifiers sitting in the staging database as a latent isolation hazard. Correcting the binding is a repair of a seeding error, not an expansion of authority.
owner_authorization.scope: the single row provider_key=meta_whatsapp_cloud AND channel=whatsapp in the dedicated staging project, and no other row in any environment

owner_proof.role: Supplies the OLD (production) identity digests that define the only writable pre-state.
owner_proof.enforcement: The operator refuses a path that resolves inside the repository, so this proof cannot be normalised into the repo by convenience.
owner_proof.note: The file is written with a UTF-8 BOM; the operator strips it before parsing. Three distinct digests are required — a proof that collapses two roles onto one digest is refused, because it could not distinguish a production-WABA binding from a production-phone binding.

staging_asset_identity.pin_source: IMPORTED from scripts/mvp/communication/create-meta-staging-vendor-onboarding-reminder-once.mjs (EXPECTED_IDENTITY_DIGESTS), not re-declared, so R7B and R7C can never drift apart

written_columns.business_account_reference: the staging WABA id, proven by digest against waba_id_sha256
written_columns.phone_number_reference: the staging phone number id, proven by digest against phone_number_id_sha256

execution_contract.unknown_flag_behaviour: REFUSED — never silently ignored, so a typo cannot degrade to a dry run reported as success
execution_contract.environment_fence: resolveStagingTarget() imported from the audited 40.12 seed; runs BEFORE any Supabase client is constructed and refuses the production and Jarvis project refs by ref, not by label
refused_pre_states: ABSENT — creation belongs to the audited 40.12 seed
SEND_CAPABLE — readiness_status = provider_ready, checked before binding
REFERENCES_NULL — deferred to the seed's NORMALIZED_DISABLED path
execution_contract.cas_predicate: provider_key + channel + the exact OLD business_account_reference + the exact OLD phone_number_reference + readiness_status <> provider_ready
execution_contract.cas_note: If the row changed between the read and the write, zero rows update and the operator reports CAS_LOST rather than overwriting an unreviewed state.
post_state_requirements: both references digest-match the staging pins
execution_contract.cannot_make_account_send_capable: The patch contains only the two reference columns. No readiness, configuration, webhook, health, billing, verification or phone-number-status column is expressible, and the port itself throws PATCH_SHAPE_REFUSED on any other shape.
execution_contract.idempotence: A rerun classifies the pre-state first. If the row already carries the staging identity the operator reports ALREADY_REBOUND and exits with zero writes, so the authority closes itself.

structural_guarantees.note: These are properties of the FILE, asserted by the validator against comment-stripped source, so prose in the header can neither satisfy nor defeat them.

downstream_state_after_rebind.note: Rebinding is necessary but NOT sufficient for the R7 canary. It clears the ACCOUNT_MISSING plan-time refusal only. The remaining R7 blockers are unchanged and are not addressed here: qf_vendor_onboarding_reminder_v1 is PENDING (not APPROVED) on the staging WABA, and code_verification_status on the staging phone is NOT_VERIFIED, which still yields READINESS_EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT.

dry_run_record.confirms: The R7A diagnosis is reproduced exactly: one row, not send-capable, still carrying the production asset references. The pre-state is the single writable one, so the guarded UPDATE is the correct and sufficient repair.
dry_run_record.known_defect_corrected: The first dry run printed the correct RESULT line and then aborted the Node runtime during teardown — 'Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING)' — because process.exit() was called while supabase-js/undici sockets were mid-close on Windows, so the shell observed exit code 127 despite a clean read-only run. An exit code that contradicts the printed result is a correctness bug in an auditable authority, so the CLI now sets process.exitCode and lets the loop drain. The pre-client refusal paths still exit immediately, which is safe because they hold no open handle.

execution_record.note: No write has been performed. The authority is committed in its unspent state. Execution requires both --execute and --owner-authorized-once-rebind, and this artifact is updated in place with the measured outcome once that run happens.
